tasks.title: 3-tier agency schema + atomic provisioning
tasks.notes: REMAINING: agency authz policy, AgencyRole runtime validation, denormalized agencyId + cross-agency invariant on agent-owned models, agency-isolation tests.

prep.what: Finish the Agency governance layer: authz policy, AgencyRole validation, and `agencyId` denormalized on every agent-facing model.
prep.understand: The 3-tier structure (Agency → Tenant → User) and `provisionAgencyOfOne` already exist and work. What remains is ENFORCEMENT: who can act across tenants within an agency, `AgencyRole` runtime checking at API boundaries, and every Prisma model that an agent touches carrying `agencyId` as a denormalized FK — the defense-in-depth isolation guarantee from PRD §2.
approach: Run `test:tenants` to confirm the 13-assertion baseline green, then open `schema.prisma` and `lib/db.ts` to audit which agent-facing models are missing `agencyId`.
Add `AgencyRole` enum (OWNER / MEMBER / VIEWER) to schema and a runtime `assertAgencyRole(userId, agencyId, minRole)` guard in a new `lib/agency-authz.ts`.

Denormalize `agencyId` on every model in `TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS` missing it; add application-level cross-agency guard (child.agencyId === parent.agencyId) consistent with the provisioning pattern from `provisionAgencyOfOne`.
Write agency-isolation tests: cross-agency read/write via `dbAdmin` is caught at the application guard; all assertions pass before marking done.

tasks.title: pending_outbound approval state machine (Phase 2)
tasks.notes: REMAINING: approve/decline/expire transitions, authenticated one-time token consumption, claim->deliver->mark-sent worker.

prep.what: Wire the approve/decline/expire state transitions for PendingOutbound — the only human gate that allows an external send.
prep.understand: Foundation is solid (7 checks green): PendingOutbound model, two DB CHECKs, `queueForApproval`, `assertDispatchable`. Phase 2 adds the state machine ON TOP: `approve` consumes the one-time `approvalTokenHash` atomically (check hash + not expired + `consumedAt IS NULL`, then set `consumedAt=now()` + `approvedByUserId`), `decline`, `expire` sweep. Then the Inngest `deliverApprovedOutbound` worker: re-assertDispatchable (race guard) → ChannelRouter.send() → mark 'sent'. The at-most-once guarantee comes entirely from `consumedAt` being set in a single atomic UPDATE.
approach: Build `approveOutbound(tokenHash)` as a DB transaction: verify hash match + `expiresAt` not past + `consumedAt IS NULL`, then single UPDATE setting `consumedAt=now()` and `approvedByUserId`.
Add `declineOutbound(id, reason)` and a scheduled `expireStaleOutbound()` sweep (Inngest cron or manual trigger for rows past `expiresAt`).
Create the Inngest `deliverApprovedOutbound` job: re-run `assertDispatchable` at dispatch time (guards race), call `channelRouter.send()`, mark `status='sent'`.
Extend test:outbound to cover: double-consume returns error, expired token rejected, approve→dispatch fires exactly once (idempotency key on the Inngest event).
resources: test:outbound suite (7 existing assertions as baseline)

tasks.title: Conversation + Message models (PWA chat history + audit)
tasks.notes: No blocking dependencies. Unblocks t15 (PWA shell) and t17 (echo loop). Both models need agencyId per PRD §2 agency invariant.

prep.what: Add Conversation and Message to Prisma — the persistence backbone for Phase 1 PWA chat and the compliance audit trail.
prep.understand: `Conversation {tenantId, agencyId, type, title}` and `Message {conversationId, tenantId, agencyId, author(agent|user), role, content, toolName?, metadata json}`. Both must be in `TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS` (ALS guard auto-scopes all reads/writes) AND carry `agencyId` per the PRD §2 invariant. Message.agencyId is denormalized from Conversation — copy it at insert time, don't FK it independently. These models unblock t15 (PWA shell), t17 (echo loop), and the t13 orchestrator streaming work.
approach: Add `Conversation` and `Message` in `schema.prisma`, mirroring how `ActivityLog` is defined — Tenant FK + Agency FK + required fields per the t29 notes in `.claude/todos.json`.
Register both in `TENANT_SCOPED_MODELS` in `lib/db.ts`; run `test:tenants` immediately — if they fail, the ALS guard isn't covering them and isolation is broken.
Run `npx prisma migrate dev --name add-conversation-message` and verify clean migration on local PG.
Run `tsc --noEmit` (or `next build --no-lint`) — model shape errors surface fast at the type level.
resources: `schema.prisma` (mirror ActivityLog's Tenant FK + Agency FK pattern)
test:tenants suite (must stay green; this is the isolation guard oracle)
t29 notes in `.claude/todos.json` (exact full field list)

tasks.title: Secrets in .env.production (Stripe both modes, Chatwoot, mail)
tasks.notes: Pre-deploy gate — needed before t36 (DO droplet deploy) can run cleanly.

prep.what: Fill the production .env file on the VPS with all four secret groups: Stripe (live + test both), Chatwoot, and mail.
prep.understand: Four groups: (1) Stripe — `STRIPE_KEY` (test publishable), `STRIPE_SECRET` (test), `STRIPE_LIVE_KEY`, `STRIPE_LIVE_SECRET`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; (2) Chatwoot — `CHATWOOT_API_TOKEN` + `CHATWOOT_BASE_URL`; (3) mail — `MAIL_HOST/PORT/USERNAME/PASSWORD/ENCRYPTION`; (4) `APP_KEY` — may already exist from the t38 import, check before regenerating. The app loads via `--env-file .env.production` in `deploy/redeploy.sh`.
approach: SSH into azteam-vps and open `.env.production` in the app root; check whether `APP_KEY` is already set (from t38).
Fill Stripe keys: dashboard.stripe.com → Developers → API Keys (toggle between test/live for each pair); grab the webhook signing secret from the endpoint you'll register in t40.
Fill Chatwoot: your Chatwoot instance → Profile Settings → Access Token; set `CHATWOOT_BASE_URL` to the instance URL.
Fill mail vars; verify with `php artisan tinker --env=production` → `Mail::raw('ping', fn($m) => $m->to('test@example.com'))` after saving.
resources: `.env.example` (canonical field reference for every expected variable)
Stripe Dashboard → Developers → API Keys (separate tabs for test + live mode)
Chatwoot instance → Profile Settings → Access Token
`deploy/redeploy.sh` (verify which env file is loaded and the app root path)

tasks.title: Reconciliation gate: imported AR + recurring state matches azteam_crm ground truth
tasks.notes: BLOCKS go-live (spec §7 step 4). Must PASS before t53 (cutover_completed flag) and t40 (enable scheduler).

prep.what: Extract the CRM reconcile logic into `ReconciliationGateService` + `billing:reconcile-cutover` artisan command verifying live AR totals and recurring dates against the legacy azteam_crm ground truth.
prep.understand: `CrmImporter::reconcile()` near line 277 already computes Σ `balance_due` per client — it just needs to become a standalone, re-runnable service that: (a) compares per-client AR against azteam_crm, (b) verifies recurring projects have the right next `ProjectInstallment.due_date`, (c) prints a clear per-client diff table, (d) exits 1 on ANY mismatch. 'PASS' is the ONLY proceed signal.
approach: Create `app/Billing/ReconciliationGateService.php` — inject both the new DB (primary) and the `azteam_crm` DB connection (from `config/database.php`); move the reconcile logic here.

Scaffold `app/Console/Commands/ReconcileCutover.php` (`billing:reconcile-cutover`): call the service, render a per-client diff table via `$this->table()`, exit 1 on FAIL with a clear column comparison.
Add next-charge-date comparison: for each active recurring project in the new DB, check `ProjectInstallment.due_date` matches the azteam_crm expected value.
Run against dev first (`php artisan billing:reconcile-cutover`); confirm output is clear enough to act on before running on prod.
resources: `app/Billing/CrmImporter.php` ~line 277 (reconcile() method — source of the logic to extract)
`tests/Feature/Billing/` (add a ReconciliationGateTest to lock the output contract)

tasks.title: Build /cashflow full month-grid calendar page
tasks.notes: Completes t30 (Dashboard cashflow deferred). `calendarMonth()` data method already built — this is UI + route only.

prep.what: Build the /cashflow page: month-grid calendar with amber (due-unpaid), green (received), red (overdue) dots, and a day-click sheet peek linking to invoices.
prep.understand: `ReceivablesDashboardService::calendarMonth($y, $m, $canPayments)` is already built and returns the calendar data — this task is pure UI + routing. The shadcn `Calendar` (react-day-picker v9) uses `DayButton` + `modifiers` to color days. Day-click triggers a shadcn `Sheet` showing that day's invoice rows with links to `/invoices/{id}`. approach: Add `CashflowController@index`: call `calendarMonth($year, $month, auth()->user()->can('payments.view'))`, pass data as Inertia props (year, month, days[]).
Register `Route::get('/cashflow', [CashflowController::class, 'index'])->middleware(['auth', 'permission:invoices.view'])->name('cashflow.index')` in `routes/web.php`.

Build `resources/js/pages/cashflow/index.tsx`: import `Calendar` from `@/components/ui/calendar`, compute `modifiers` from the days prop (amber/green/red), add `Sheet` on day-click with the invoice list.
Add a sidebar nav item and a Feature test asserting the page renders for `invoices.view` and returns 403 without it.
